prerequisites: Basic subjects from the first two years of the degree (physics, chemistry, mathematics, industrial drawing, and manufacturing processes)

learning_outcomes.text: To know and adequately use different measuring instruments and equipment.
To identify and select the most appropriate instrument based on different metrological and economic aspects.
To elaborate calibration procedures and estimate measurement uncertainties.
To organize and manage a metrology laboratory.
To elaborate and manage inspection plans, quality improvement, stability and capability of manufacturing processes.

syllabus_topics: Identification, selection, and use of measuring equipment
Length measurement. Calipers and Micrometers
Angle measurement
Materialization of units and shapes. Standards and templates
Indirect and comparative measurements. Shape verification
Measurement of other magnitudes and their measurement systems
Quality Control Techniques with Non-Destructive Testing (NDT)
Coordinate measurement
Coordinate Measuring Machines (CMM)
Coordinate Measuring Arms (CMA, AACMM)
Non-contact digitization instruments and techniques
Calculation and expression of measurement uncertainty
Influence quantities and error propagation. Traceability and Calibration
Calculation of measurement uncertainty
Calibration procedures
Management and organization of metrology laboratories
Management of metrology laboratories. Calibration plan
Testing and Calibration Laboratories. Accreditation bodies
Quality control and management in manufacturing
Automated measurement and inspection systems
Elaboration of inspection plans. Measurement assurance
Statistical Process Control (SPC)
Quality Management. Six-Sigma and Lean Manufacturing methodology

assessment_methods.method: Final project, with presentation and defense
Attendance and participation in Laboratory practices and Classroom practices (deliverables, virtual campus, etc.)

assessment_rules: The final grade is a weighted combination of a theoretical-practical exam (70%) and practical block activities (30%). The theoretical-practical exam requires a minimum score of 4 out of 10 points. If this minimum is not met, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4. The practical block activities grade is retained for all official calls within the academic year.
